status_reason: Full text incl. appendices read; gene construction procedure absent from paper.

paper.title: From Procedural Skills to Strategy Genes: Towards Experience-Driven Test-Time Evolution
paper.central_claim: Reusable experience should be encoded as a compact control-oriented object (strategy Gene under GEP) rather than documentation-style Skill packages; Gene is a better test-time control signal and a better carrier for iterative experience accumulation.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; null by design (no probing).

rationale: Gene vs Skill probes on in-house scenarios and an Evolver CritPt run. Deltas of 0.5-3 pp with no repeats while a repeated baseline moves 2.2 pp on Pro; per-scenario experience tested on same scenario; Evolver gain lacks gene-off control. Level task; scoped.

missing_sections: numeric content of Figures 2-5 not in text (Fig.5 values are given in the caption/text)
gene/skill construction procedure (psi) is not in the paper, only a pointer to an external repository
per-cell trial counts and variance not reported

evidence.quote: This beta technical report asks how reusable experience should be represented
evidence.support_explanation: Status of the work: beta technical report.

evidence.quote: We study this question in 4,590 controlled trials across 45 scientific code-solving scenarios.
evidence.support_explanation: Scale of the controlled study.

evidence.quote: A compact Gene representation yields the strongest overall average, remains competitive under substantial structural perturbations, and outperforms
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim on representation.

evidence.quote: Taken together, these studies reinforce a stronger assumption about reusable experience: more complete and structured experience representations should be more beneficial for subsequent task solving.
evidence.support_explanation: Assumption audited by the paper.

evidence.quote: Our point of departure is to test this assumption directly.
evidence.support_explanation: Operation: audit the assumption.

evidence.quote: their primary focus remains on how experience can be accumulated, maintained, or evolved once externalized
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap vs neighbours (ProcMEM, MemSkill, Memento-Skills, CoWork-X, streaming memory): representation of the object is the missing question. Compact lesson stores such as ReasoningBank or Dynamic Cheatsheet are not discussed.

evidence.quote: Accordingly, a strategy gene is not merely a compressed version of a procedural skill, but a different abstraction of reusable experience.
evidence.support_explanation: The distillation map from skill/trajectories to gene is described only as psi; no model, prompt or human involvement is specified.

evidence.quote: Skill denotes the full documentation-style skill package, including the main skill document together with auxiliary scripts, notes, and references
evidence.support_explanation: The Skill baseline is the authors own package built for each scenario, not an existing third-party skill library.

evidence.quote: all derived from the same per-scenario experience source
evidence.support_explanation: Experience (and hence Gene/Skill) is per scenario; test scenarios coincide with the experience source scenarios.

evidence.quote: Two representative failure modes are to treat min_distance as a wavelength value rather than converting it into sample-index units before calling scipy.signal.find_peaks
evidence.support_explanation: Gene content encodes the scenario-specific failure modes that the scenario checkpoints then test (FWHM, peak count).
Headline: Gene +3.0 pp on the Pro/Flash mean; on Pro Gene equals no guidance, the gain is on Flash.

evidence.quote: Relative to no guidance, Gene remains nearly unchanged on Pro
evidence.support_explanation: Gene does not help the stronger model.
The no-guidance Pro score is 57.9% here but 60.1% in Tables 1-6 (avg 49.8 vs 51.0): evidence of run-to-run variation of about 2 pp on Pro, 1.2 pp on average, comparable to many reported deltas.
Matched-budget comparison: Gene +3.0 vs truncated Skill fragments +0.5/+1.0, a 2-2.5 pp gap.

evidence.quote: we truncate the selected Skill fragments to approximately 230 tokens, so that they match the prompt budget of Gene as closely as possible
evidence.support_explanation: Budget (tokens) matched; authoring effort is not: Gene is distilled, Skill fragments are truncated.

evidence.quote: Gene (keywords + summary) 51.3% 50.6% 51.0% +0.0 Gene (keywords only) 57.9% 49.1% 53.5% +2.5

evidence.support_explanation: Failure-warnings-only is best, but the baseline here is a different no-guidance run (49.8).

evidence.quote: Complementary composition is more harmful than conflicting composition.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors report negative composition results.

evidence.quote: Generation is performed with low-temperature decoding

evidence.quote: Evolution Probe studies which representational properties make genes suitable as carriers of accumulated experience, including structured-versus-static presentation, failure-aware organization, ordering of failure and strategy information, and evolution-style narrative wrappers.

gap.author_gap: Experience-reuse work optimises how experience is stored, retrieved and evolved, but assumes fuller structured skill documents are better; whether that representation works as a test-time control signal is untested.
gap.checked_gap: The audited assumption is stated by the authors and tested on their own Skill packages; the result (long documents can hurt a model) is plausible, but the Skill baseline is the authors construct (E008) and compact lesson stores that resemble Gene (ExpeL insights, ReasoningBank items, Dynamic Cheatsheet) are not treated as nearest neighbours.
gap.lineage/closest_adjacent: Reflection/critique loops, episodic and lesson memories, executable skill libraries (ProcMEM, MemSkill, Memento-Skills, CoWork-X) and streaming/meta-evolved memory (named in Sec.2.2).
gap.residue: Whether experience objects should be documentation-like or compact control objects, and whether that choice affects later evolution.
gap.stakes: Token cost and dilution of skill documents at inference.
gap.method_response: Gene object under GEP, tested by probes and an Evolver run.
gap.remaining_gap: Gene construction procedure, causal gene-off evidence for evolution, test/selection separation, variance.
gap.unresolved: Nearest neighbours were not fetched; no comparison to compact lesson stores; gene authoring process absent from the paper.

claims.text: Documentation-oriented Skill packages are unstable test-time control: only a narrow procedural slice helps.
claims.setting: 45 scenarios, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Flash Lite, 1,440 trials
claims.allowed_conclusion: For these authored Skill packages and models, adding the full package did not raise the mean; differences below about 2 pp are not distinguishable from the observed baseline variation.

claims.text: A compact Gene is the strongest overall and beats budget-matched Skill fragments.
claims.result/denominator: Gene 54.0 vs 51.0 baseline; 2-2.5 pp over short Skill fragments
claims.allowed_conclusion: Gene has the highest mean in these runs, driven by the weaker model; not distinguishable from noise or authoring effort.

claims.text: Gene is a better carrier for accumulating failure history; accumulation should be selective.
claims.selection_vs_test: static conditions, no accumulation loop run
claims.result/denominator: Gene+failure 52.0 vs Skill+failure 47.8; warnings-only 54.4 vs separate 49.8 baseline
claims.allowed_conclusion: Static prompt-format comparisons; no iterative accumulation tested in these probes.

claims.text: Gene-evolved systems improve over paired base models on CritPt (9.1 -> 18.57; 17.7 -> 27.14).
claims.setting: Evolver on OpenClaw, 70 tasks, two versions
claims.baseline/control: Gemini 3 Pro Preview / 3.1 Pro Preview base numbers
claims.result/denominator: accuracy of 70 tasks, single run per version
claims.allowed_conclusion: The evolved agent system scored higher than quoted base-model numbers; attribution to the gene representation or evolution loop is not established.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Gene/Skill conditions are applied at test time to the scenario that supplied the experience; there is no construction/evaluation split, and the Evolver result lacks a retained-artifact-off control. Gains are task-level only.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In an in-house set of 45 scenarios with two Gemini models, a compact structured prompt per scenario produced the highest mean pass rate (54.0 vs 51.0 no guidance, 49.9 full Skill package), mainly through the weaker model, with effect sizes comparable to the observed baseline variation (60.1 vs 57.9 on Pro). Author-reported, not reproduced.
assessment.unresolved: Gene authoring procedure, per-cell trial counts, uncertainty, evolution/eval separation, same-runtime gene-off control.

retention_trace.proposed_change: Gene (distilled, procedure unspecified) or GEP mutate step
retention_trace.selection: validation hooks, criteria unspecified; static probes have none
retention_trace.measured_gain: pass rate +3.0 pp mean; CritPt +9.4 pp vs quoted base

G.reason: The audited assumption (fuller skill documents are better) is stated and plausibly important, but the Skill baseline is the authors construct and compact lesson stores that resemble Gene are not treated as nearest neighbours; gap is largely framed through the Gene vs Skill contrast.

M.reason: Concrete mechanism (signal density/control orientation) with distinguishable predictions (structure-vs-content, flattening) but the key operation, distillation of Gene from Skill or trajectories, is unspecified and could carry the effect; the story for evolution is not tied to a mechanism test.

X.reason: Gene schema and GEP loop (scan, signal, intent, mutate, validate, solidify) are described at protocol level and the probe prompts are shown, but gene construction, validation criteria, selection/routing, retention and retirement, and the CritPt setup are not reproducible from the paper.

E.measurement.reason: Checkpoint pass rate from sandboxed scenario scripts is objective and the no-guidance baseline exists, but the benchmark and scripts are in-house and unaudited, the gene targets known failure checkpoints, and the CritPt base numbers are taken from elsewhere.

E.causality.reason: Token-matched fragments, content/structure perturbations and flattening give partial attribution on this benchmark; authoring effort is not matched, there is no gene-off control for the Evolver result, and noise is not separated from the claimed deltas.

E.holdout.reason: Experience is per scenario and tested on the same scenario; no construction/test split is stated, evolution tasks and CritPt are not shown to be disjoint, arXiv-derived genes are used, and claims about experience reuse generalise from one in-house benchmark and two models.

E.statistics.reason: Trial totals are given (4,590 retained) with negative results reported, but no per-cell counts, repeats, intervals or tests; the no-guidance Pro baseline differs by 2.2 pp between tables, comparable to many claimed deltas. Excluded trials are not accounted for.

E.cost.reason: Prompt-token budgets are explicit (230 vs 2,500) and matched for fragments; an end-to-end cost is given for one run, but it counts observable I/O tokens only and excludes the two-day evolution, gene mining and failed trials.
